question: In its communication ‘A Simpler, Clearer and Better Enforced EU Rulebook’, the Commission proposes a new simplification platform to support the action plan for a comprehensive regulatory review. According to the communication, this platform focuses exclusively on the following policy priorities: goods and services, financial services, customs, taxation, health and food safety, agriculture, transport, energy, climate, environment, digital, housing and permitting. 1.

If this list is exhaustive, why does the Commission focus only on these policy areas and not on other key policy areas where simplification is urgently needed, such as: competition policy (State aid, mergers and acquisitions), the common commercial policy with regard to non-EU countries, economic policy (e.g. the European Semester), employment and social policy (e.g.

labour law, working conditions and social inclusion), consumer protection and justice and home affairs (e.g. judicial cooperation, cooperation in civil and criminal matters and police and security cooperation)?

Does the Commission consider these policy areas not to be a priority? This question is all the more pertinent since the Union’s Treaty-based competences in areas such as common commercial policy and competition policy are considerably broader than its limited competences in areas such as customs, taxation and housing.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.9.2026) The Commission communication ‘A Simpler, Clearer and Better Enforced EU Rulebook’1 states that a key action will be ‘setting up a new high-level expert group – the Simplification Platform – to support simplification and burden reduction efforts.

’ The communication does not state that the Platform will limit itself to any specific area of EU law or policy in its works. According to the Commission communication, the Platform will support the regulatory deep cleaning efforts, but these efforts will not be its exclusive focus.

As explained in the communication, the Regulatory Deep Cleaning Action Plan focuses on 12 priority areas, selected based on internal analysis of implementation challenges and on stakeholder input, including in implementation dialogues and reality checks.
